title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Rules for Arithmetic Operations with Significant Figures
text:
Rules for Arithmetic Operations with Significant Figures

Key terms: Significant Figure, Multiplication, Division, Addition, Subtraction

In multiplication or division, the final result should retain as many significant figures as the original number with the least significant figures. In addition or subtraction, the final result should retain as many decimal places as the number with the least decimal places.

metadata.topic: Rules for Arithmetic Operations with Significant Figures

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Rounding Off Measurements
text:
Rounding Off Measurements

Key terms: significant figures, rounding off, approximate numbers

When dealing with approximate numbers, round off the result to the appropriate significant figures. The rule is to raise the preceding digit by 1 if the insignificant digit to be dropped is more than 5, and leave it unchanged if it's less than 5. If the preceding digit is even and the insignificant digit is 5, simply drop it. In complex calculations, retain one more significant figure in intermediate steps.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Rounding Off Measurements in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Determining Uncertainty in Results
text:
Determining Uncertainty in Results

Key terms: uncertainty, error, least precise measurement

When combining measurements, the uncertainty or error in the final result depends on the least precise measurement. For addition and subtraction, the rule is to keep the same number of decimal places as the least precise measurement. For multiplication and division, the rule is to add the number of decimal places in the original measurements.

metadata.subject: Physics

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Dimensions of Physical Quantities

Dimensions of Physical Quantities

Physical quantities can be expressed in terms of seven fundamental or base quantities: length [L], mass [M], time [T], electric current [A], thermodynamic temperature [K], luminous intensity [cd], and amount of substance [mol]. Dimensional analysis helps in checking the consistency of equations and deducing relations among physical quantities. Physical quantities on both sides of an equation must have the same dimensions. Only quantities with the same physical dimensions can be added or subtracted.

Impulse

Circular Motion - Centripetal Force

Motion of Car on Level and Banked Road

Newton's First Law of Motion

An object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion stays in motion with constant velocity, unless acted upon by an external force.

Momentum

Newton's Second Law of Motion

The net force acting on an object is equal to its mass times its acceleration (F = ma). It is a vector equation applicable to a particle or a system of particles.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Newton's Second Law of Motion in Grade 11 Physics.

Impulse

Newton's Third Law of Motion

For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. Forces in nature always occur between pairs of bodies.

Law of Conservation of Momentum

The total momentum of an isolated system of particles is conserved. It follows from Newton's second and third laws of motion.

Friction

Frictional force opposes (impending or actual) relative motion between two surfaces in contact. It is independent of the area of contact and depends on the coefficients of static and kinetic friction.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Free-Body Diagrams
text:
Free-Body Diagrams

A free-body diagram is a sketch of all the forces acting on a single object in a problem. It helps in solving problems in mechanics by clearly defining the system and considering all forces on it.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Free-Body Diagrams in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Scalar Product of Vectors
text:
Scalar Product of Vectors

Key terms: dot product, scalar product, cosine of angle

The dot product of two vectors, a scalar quantity calculated as the product of their magnitudes and the cosine of the angle between them. It's a measure of how much the vectors are pointing in the same direction.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Scalar Product of Vectors in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Work Done by a Force
text:
Work Done by a Force

Key terms: work, force, displacement, angle

Work is done when a force acts on an object and causes it to move. It's calculated as the product of the force, the displacement, and the cosine of the angle between them.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Work Done by a Force in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Kinetic Energy
text:
Kinetic Energy

Key terms: kinetic energy, mass, velocity

The energy possessed by an object due to its motion. It's calculated as half the mass of the object times the square of its velocity.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Kinetic Energy in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Work-Energy Theorem
text:
Work-Energy Theorem

Key terms: work-energy theorem, kinetic energy, net force

The change in kinetic energy of an object is equal to the work done on it by the net force acting on it. This is a fundamental principle in physics.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Work-Energy Theorem in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Work Done by a Variable Force
text:
Work Done by a Variable Force

Key terms: variable force, integral, displacement

For a variable force, the work done is the integral of the force over the displacement. This is a more general form of the work done formula for constant forces.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Work Done by a Variable Force
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Work Done by a Variable Force in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Work-Energy Theorem
text:
Work-Energy Theorem

Key terms: work, kinetic energy, force

The work done by a force is equal to the change in kinetic energy of the object it acts upon. This principle is useful in solving problems where forces are variable.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Work-Energy Theorem in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Potential Energy
text:
Potential Energy

Key terms: potential energy, work, force

Potential energy is the 'stored' energy by virtue of the position or configuration of a body. It is the negative of the work done by the force in raising the object to that height.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Potential Energy in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Conservation of Mechanical Energy
text:
Conservation of Mechanical Energy

Key terms: mechanical energy, conservative force, kinetic energy, potential energy

The total mechanical energy of a system is conserved if the forces doing work on it are conservative. This means the sum of kinetic and potential energies remains constant.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Conservation of Mechanical Energy in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Spring Potential Energy
text:
Spring Potential Energy

Key terms: potential energy, spring constant, displacement

The potential energy of a spring is given by V(x) = (1/2)kx^2, where k is the spring constant and x is the displacement from the equilibrium position.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Spring Potential Energy in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Maximum Speed in a Spring
text:
Maximum Speed in a Spring

Key terms: maximum speed, spring constant, mass

The maximum speed of an object attached to a spring and released from rest is given by v_max = sqrt(k/m), where k is the spring constant and m is the mass of the object.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Maximum Speed in a Spring in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Conservation of Mechanical Energy
text:
Conservation of Mechanical Energy

Key terms: mechanical energy, kinetic energy, potential energy

In a closed system, the total mechanical energy (kinetic + potential) remains constant. This principle is often depicted graphically.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Conservation of Mechanical Energy in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Maximum Compression of a Spring
text:
Maximum Compression of a Spring

Key terms: maximum compression, kinetic energy, potential energy, spring constant

In a collision between a moving object and a spring, the maximum compression of the spring occurs when the kinetic energy of the object is entirely converted into potential energy of the spring.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Maximum Compression of a Spring in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Non-Conservative Forces
text:
Non-Conservative Forces

Key terms: non-conservative forces, friction, conservation of energy

Not all forces are conservative. Friction, for example, is a non-conservative force. The principle of conservation of energy must be modified in such cases.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Non-Conservative Forces in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Power
text:
Power

Key terms: power, work, energy, watts, horsepower

Power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred. It is a scalar quantity with dimensions [ML2T–3] and units of watts (W) or horsepower (hp).

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Power in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Elastic and Inelastic Collisions
text:
Elastic and Inelastic Collisions

Key terms: elastic collision, inelastic collision, linear momentum, kinetic energy

In a collision, the total linear momentum is conserved, but the total kinetic energy is not necessarily conserved. Elastic collisions conserve kinetic energy, while inelastic collisions do not.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Elastic and Inelastic Collisions in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | One-Dimensional Collisions
text:
One-Dimensional Collisions

Key terms: one-dimensional collision, momentum, kinetic energy, final velocity

In a one-dimensional collision, the momentum and kinetic energy of the system are conserved. The final velocities of the colliding objects can be determined using these principles.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to One-Dimensional Collisions in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Two-Dimensional Collisions
text:
Two-Dimensional Collisions

Key terms: two-dimensional collision, momentum, final velocity, angle

In a two-dimensional collision, the momentum of the system is conserved in all three directions. The final velocities and angles of the colliding objects can be determined using these principles.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Two-Dimensional Collisions in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Scattering
text:
Scattering

Key terms: scattering, momentum, energy, velocity, direction

Scattering involves forces acting at a distance, unlike collisions which occur only when bodies touch each other. The velocities and directions in which particles move after scattering can be determined using principles of conservation of momentum and energy.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Scattering in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Work-Energy Theorem
text:
Work-Energy Theorem

Key terms: work, energy, kinetic energy, net force

The change in kinetic energy of a body is equal to the work done by the net force on the body. This means that the work done by a force is equal to the change in kinetic energy of the body due to that force.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Work-Energy Theorem in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Conservative Force
text:
Conservative Force

Key terms: conservative force, path independence, potential energy

A force is conservative if the work done by it on an object is path independent and depends only on the end points, or if the work done by the force is zero for an arbitrary closed path taken by the object such that it returns to its initial position.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Conservative Force in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Potential Energy
text:
Potential Energy

Key terms: potential energy, force field, configuration

Potential energy is a type of energy possessed by an object due to its position or configuration. It is the energy that an object has due to its location in a force field or its configuration, such as being stretched or compressed.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Potential Energy in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Conservation of Mechanical Energy
text:
Conservation of Mechanical Energy

Key terms: mechanical energy, conservative forces, potential energy, kinetic energy

The total mechanical energy of a body remains constant if the only forces that act on the body are conservative. This means that the sum of the potential energy and kinetic energy of a body remains constant if only conservative forces act on it.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Conservation of Mechanical Energy in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Gravitational Potential Energy
text:
Gravitational Potential Energy

Key terms: gravitational potential energy, gravity, height

The gravitational potential energy of a particle of mass m at a height x about the earth’s surface is given by V(x) = m g x, where g is the acceleration due to gravity and is assumed to be constant.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Gravitational Potential Energy in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Elastic Potential Energy
text:
Elastic Potential Energy

Key terms: elastic potential energy, spring, force constant, extension

The elastic potential energy of a spring of force constant k and extension x is given by V(x) = 1/2 k x^2. This energy is stored in the spring when it is compressed or stretched from its equilibrium position.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Elastic Potential Energy in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Scalar (Dot) Product of Vectors
text:
Scalar (Dot) Product of Vectors

Key terms: scalar product, dot product, vectors, angle

The scalar or dot product of two vectors A and B is a scalar quantity given by A.B = AB cos q, where q is the angle between A and B. It can be positive, negative, or zero depending upon the value of q.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Scalar (Dot) Product of Vectors in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Work Done by Friction
text:
Work Done by Friction

Key terms: work done by friction, kinetic energy, loss in energy

The work done by friction on a moving body is negative, meaning that friction opposes the motion of the body. The work done by friction is equal to the loss in kinetic energy of the body.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Work Done by Friction in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Centre of Mass of a System of Particles
text:
Centre of Mass of a System of Particles

Key terms: centre of mass, mass, position

The centre of mass is a point that represents the entire system's mass distribution. It's calculated as the mass-weighted average of the particles' positions. For a system of n particles with masses m1, m2, ..., mn and positions (x1, y1, z1), (x2, y2, z2), ..., (xn, yn, zn), the centre of mass (X, Y, Z) is given by X = ∑(mi * xi) / ∑mi, Y = ∑(mi * yi) / ∑mi, Z = ∑(mi * zi) / ∑mi.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Centre of Mass of a System of Particles
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Centre of Mass of a System of Particles in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Motion of a Rigid Body
text:
Motion of a Rigid Body

Key terms: rigid body, translation, rotation, axis

A rigid body's motion can be either pure translation (all particles move with the same velocity) or a combination of translation and rotation. If a rigid body is pivoted or fixed, its motion is rotation, which can be about a fixed or moving axis.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Motion of a Rigid Body in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Rotational Motion about a Fixed Axis
text:
Rotational Motion about a Fixed Axis

Key terms: rotational motion, fixed axis, circle, radius

Rotational motion about a fixed axis involves every particle of the body moving in a circle with its centre on the axis. The axis is perpendicular to the plane of the circle. The radius of the circle is the perpendicular distance of the particle from the axis.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Rotational Motion about a Fixed Axis
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Rotational Motion about a Fixed Axis in Grade 11 Physics.

Centre of Mass (CM) for Homogeneous Bodies

For homogeneous bodies of regular shapes like rings, discs, spheres, rods, the centre of mass lies at their geometric centre due to symmetry.

metadata.topic: Centre of Mass (CM) for Homogeneous Bodies
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Centre of Mass (CM) for Homogeneous Bodies in Grade 11 Physics.

text:
Centre of Mass (CM) for Thin Rods

Key terms: centre of mass, geometric centre, thin rod, reflection symmetry

For a thin rod, the centre of mass coincides with its geometric centre due to reflection symmetry.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Centre of Mass (CM) for Thin Rods
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Centre of Mass (CM) for Thin Rods in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Centre of Mass (CM) for Particles in Equilateral Triangle
text:
Centre of Mass (CM) for Particles in Equilateral Triangle

Key terms: centre of mass, equilateral triangle, particles, masses, positions

The centre of mass of three particles at the vertices of an equilateral triangle is not at the geometric centre but at a point determined by the masses and positions of the particles.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Centre of Mass (CM) for Particles in Equilateral Triangle
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Centre of Mass (CM) for Particles in Equilateral Triangle in Grade 11 Physics.

Centre of Mass (CM) for Triangular Lamina

Key terms: centre of mass, triangular lamina, centroid, medians

The centre of mass of a triangular lamina lies at the centroid, the point of concurrence of the medians.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Centre of Mass (CM) for Triangular Lamina
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Centre of Mass (CM) for Triangular Lamina in Grade 11 Physics.

text:
Motion of Centre of Mass

The centre of mass of a system of particles moves as if all the mass of the system was concentrated at the centre of mass and all the external forces were applied at that point.

metadata.subject: Physics

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Linear Momentum of a System of Particles

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles

The total linear momentum of a system of particles is equal to the product of the total mass of the system and the velocity of its centre of mass.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Vector Product of Two Vectors
text:
Vector Product of Two Vectors

Key terms: vector product, cross product, magnitude, direction

A vector product of two vectors a and b is a vector c such that its magnitude is c = a * b * sin(θ), where a and b are magnitudes of a and b, and θ is the angle between the two vectors. The vector c is perpendicular to the plane containing a and b, and its direction is given by the right-hand screw rule.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Vector Product of Two Vectors in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Moment of a Force (Torque)
text:
Moment of a Force (Torque)

Key terms: moment of force, torque, vector product, magnitude, direction

The moment of a force acting on a particle with respect to a point is the vector product of the position vector of the particle and the force. It is a vector quantity that is perpendicular to the plane containing the position vector and the force, and its direction is given by the right-hand screw rule. Its magnitude is given by the formula τ = r * F * sin(θ), where r is the magnitude of the position vector, F is the magnitude of the force, and θ is the angle between the position vector and the force.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Moment of a Force (Torque) in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Angular Velocity and Linear Velocity
text:
Angular Velocity and Linear Velocity

Key terms: angular velocity, linear velocity, relation, direction

In rotational motion, the angular velocity (ω) is related to the linear velocity (v) of a particle by the formula v = ω * r, where r is the perpendicular distance of the particle from the axis of rotation. The angular velocity is a vector quantity that lies along the axis of rotation and points in the direction in which a right-hand screw would advance if the head of the screw is rotated with the body.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Angular Velocity and Linear Velocity in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Angular Acceleration
text:
Angular Acceleration

Angular acceleration (α) is the time rate of change of angular velocity (ω). If the axis of rotation is fixed, the direction of α is fixed, and the vector equation reduces to a scalar equation. Angular acceleration is defined as d(ω)/dt.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Angular Acceleration in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Moment of Force (Torque)
text:
Moment of Force (Torque)

Torque is the rotational analogue of force in linear motion. It's a vector product of force and the perpendicular distance from the force's line of action to the axis of rotation. It causes an object to rotate.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Moment of Force (Torque) in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Angular Momentum
text:
Angular Momentum

Key terms: angular momentum, linear momentum, conservation of angular momentum

Angular momentum is the rotational analogue of linear momentum. It's a vector product of linear momentum and the position vector of the particle. It's conserved when the net external torque is zero.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Angular Momentum in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Relation between Torque and Angular Momentum
text:
Relation between Torque and Angular Momentum

The time rate of change of angular momentum is equal to the torque acting on the particle. This is the rotational analogue of Newton's second law (F = dp/dt).

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Relation between Torque and Angular Momentum
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Relation between Torque and Angular Momentum in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Conservation of Angular Momentum
text:
Conservation of Angular Momentum

Key terms: conservation of angular momentum, external torque, total angular momentum

If the total external torque on a system of particles is zero, then the total angular momentum of the system is conserved, i.e., it remains constant.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Conservation of Angular Momentum in Grade 11 Physics.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body

Key terms: mechanical equilibrium, total force, total torque

A rigid body is in mechanical equilibrium if both its linear momentum and angular momentum are not changing with time. This means the total force and total torque on the body are zero.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Couple or Torque

A couple is a pair of forces of equal magnitude but acting in opposite directions with different lines of action. It produces rotation without translation.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Couple and Moment of a Couple
text:
Couple and Moment of a Couple

Key terms: couple, moment of a couple, line of action

A couple is a pair of equal and opposite forces acting along parallel lines but not along the same line of action. The moment of a couple is the product of the magnitude of either force and the perpendicular distance between the lines of action of the forces, and it is independent of the point about which the moments are taken.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Principle of Moments (Lever)
text:
Principle of Moments (Lever)

Key terms: principle of moments, lever, mechanical advantage

The principle of moments states that for a lever in equilibrium, the sum of the moments of the forces acting on it must be zero. This means that the effort arm × effort = load arm × load. The mechanical advantage of a lever is the ratio of the load to the effort.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Principle of Moments (Lever) in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Centre of Gravity
text:
Centre of Gravity

Key terms: centre of gravity, centre of mass, gravitational torque

The centre of gravity (CG) of an object is the point where the total torque due to the forces of gravity on the individual particles that make up the object is zero. It coincides with the centre of mass in uniform gravity or gravity-free space.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Centre of Gravity in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Moment of Inertia
text:
Moment of Inertia

Key terms: moment of inertia, rotational motion, angular velocity

The moment of inertia is a measure of the resistance of a rotating body to changes in its rotational motion. It is the rotational analogue of mass in linear motion and is defined as the sum of the products of the mass of each particle in the body and the square of its distance from the axis of rotation.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Moment of Inertia in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Moment of Inertia and Radius of Gyration
text:
Moment of Inertia and Radius of Gyration

Key terms: moment of inertia, radius of gyration, mass, shape, size, mass distribution, axis of rotation

Moment of inertia (I) measures a body's resistance to changes in its rotation rate. It depends on the body's mass, shape, size, mass distribution, and axis of rotation. The radius of gyration (k) is a geometric property that, when multiplied by the body's mass, gives its moment of inertia about a specific axis.

Units of Moment of Inertia

Key terms: dimensions, SI units, kg, m²

The dimensions of moment of inertia are ML², and its SI units are kg m². This means that moment of inertia is measured in kilograms times meters squared.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Flywheel in Machines
text:
Flywheel in Machines

Key terms: flywheel, rotational energy, sudden changes, gradual change, smooth ride

A flywheel is a rotating mechanical device that stores rotational energy. It resists sudden changes in rotational speed, allowing for a gradual change in speed and preventing jerky motions. This ensures a smooth ride in vehicles and other machines.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Angular Displacement, Velocity, and Acceleration
text:
Angular Displacement, Velocity, and Acceleration

Key terms: angular displacement, angular velocity, angular acceleration, analogy, translational motion

Angular displacement (θ) is the change in the orientation of a rotating body. Angular velocity (ω) is the rate of change of angular displacement, and angular acceleration (α) is the rate of change of angular velocity. These quantities are analogous to linear displacement, velocity, and acceleration in translational motion.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Angular Displacement, Velocity, and Acceleration in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Kinematic Equations of Rotational Motion
text:
Kinematic Equations of Rotational Motion

Key terms: kinematic equations, rotational motion, uniform angular acceleration, analogy, linear motion

The kinematic equations for rotational motion with uniform angular acceleration are: ω = ω₀ + αt, θ = θ₀ + ω₀t + (α/2)t², and ω² = ω₀² + 2α(θ - θ₀). These equations are analogous to the kinematic equations for linear motion with uniform acceleration.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Kinematic Equations of Rotational Motion in Grade 11 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Work Done by a Torque
text:
Work Done by a Torque

Key terms: work done, torque, fixed axis, analogy, force, linear motion, kinetic energy

Work done by a torque (τ) acting on a body rotating about a fixed axis is given by W = τθ. This is analogous to the work done by a force (F) acting on a body in linear motion, which is given by W = Fd. The rate of work done is equal to the rate of increase of kinetic energy.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Angular Momentum in Rotational Motion

Key terms: angular momentum, rigid body, fixed axis, moment of inertia, angular velocity, external torque

The angular momentum (L) of a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis is given by L = Iω, where I is the moment of inertia and ω is the angular velocity. The time rate of change of angular momentum is equal to the total external torque acting on the body.

The angular momentum of a particle is given by the cross product of its position vector and linear momentum. It's a vector quantity that measures the particle's tendency to rotate around a point.

In the absence of external torques, the total angular momentum of a closed system remains constant. This is the principle of conservation of angular momentum.

The centre of mass is a point where the entire mass of an object is assumed to be concentrated. It's calculated as the sum of the products of each particle's mass and its position vector, divided by the total mass.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Cross Product

The cross product of two vectors is a vector that is perpendicular to both of the original vectors. Its magnitude is the product of the magnitudes of the original vectors and the sine of the angle between them.

When a beam is balanced, the mass of one section times its distance from the fulcrum equals the mass of another section times its distance from the fulcrum. This can be used to find the mass of the beam itself.
